global.title: ArianeGroup launches 36 more Amazon Leo satellites on tenth Ariane 6 flight
global.summary: ArianeGroup says Ariane 6 carried another 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit on its tenth flight. The mission is VA271. The window had moved from the twenty-third of November to the twenty-fourth. Amazon's earlier Leo launch on a Vulcan rocket failed on the fifteenth of November. The cause of that failure and the date of the next Vulcan flight are not known.
global.why: A European launcher has delivered a large commercial constellation batch on a rescheduled date. The Rome meeting on the fifteenth of December is the next European policy date.
global.bar: Company statement only; no independent confirmation of orbit insertion in hand.

global.title: China launches Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, its first foreign astronaut
global.summary: A Pakistani astronaut has launched into space aboard a Chinese rocket. Spanish press describes him as the first foreign astronaut admitted to China's space station. The launch took place on the twenty-fifth of November. Mission length and duties are not given.
global.why: China is opening its station to a South Asian partner. That widens its list of space partners beyond Russia.

global.title: ESA reports BepiColombo in Mercury orbit despite unexpected challenge
global.summary: ESA says BepiColombo is safely in orbit around Mercury. The agency refers to an unexpected challenge. Spanish trade coverage mentions a fault on board. The science start date is not known. The arrival was first filed on the eighteenth of November.
global.why: The probe has reached its orbit but the nature of the fault is not public. The science start date will show how serious it is.
global.bar: Fault detail from Spanish trade headline only.

global.title: ULA Vulcan suffers anomaly on first Amazon Leo launch
global.summary: A ULA Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly on its first Amazon Leo launch on the fifteenth of November. The cause is not known. The date of the next flight is not known.
global.why: Amazon's constellation has lost one launch provider for now. Ariane 6 has delivered its batch.

items.title: European Commission recommends five-fold increase in competition fund
items.summary: The vote of the tenth of November produced no outcome. The MaiaSpace contract remains unsigned. The Commission recommended on the eighteenth of November that its competition fund grow five times. Rome follows on the fifteenth of December.
items.why: Funding for European launch competition is recommended but not decided. Rome is the next point at which it can move.
items.bar: Standing situation with dated next step.

items.title: Ukraine reports more restrictions on Starshield access
items.summary: Ukraine reported further restrictions to Starshield access on the twelfth of November. SpaceX has made no statement. The hope of a replacement by mid-2027 is unchanged.
items.why: Ukraine's front-line communications depend on a service it does not control. No date is set for a change.

items.title: Swedish space agency marks Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth
items.summary: The Swedish National Space Agency notes that Voyager 1 has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth. The agency's next national event, Rymddagen, is on the eighteenth of February 2027.
items.why: The milestone was first filed on the eighteenth of November. The Swedish date is the next fixed Nordic marker.
items.bar: Standing; Rymddagen date from agency page.

items.title: Spain tests military Govsatcom access through SpainSat NG I
items.summary: Spain has tested access to Govsatcom military satellite communications through SpainSat NG I for the first time. Station and content of the test are not known.
items.why: It is a first use of the EU pooled service over a national satellite. Wider Govsatcom use is not yet dated.

items.title: Italy conditions Iceye bid for Avio on national security guarantees
items.summary: Italy has made Iceye's offer for rocket maker Avio conditional on national security guarantees. The terms of the guarantees are not known.
items.why: A launcher maker may pass to a foreign satellite company. Rome's conditions will decide whether the bid proceeds.

items.title: Amazon Leo and a Chinese rival set to enter Kazakhstan satellite internet market
items.summary: Amazon Leo and a Chinese competitor are set to enter Kazakhstan's satellite internet market. No start date is given.
items.why: Western and Chinese constellations are competing for a Central Asian market. Licensing dates are not known.

items.title: Armenia's regulator and SpaceX discuss Starlink development
items.summary: Armenia's telecom regulator and SpaceX discussed satellite internet and mobile communications. No licence or date is given.
items.why: Starlink is seeking a position in the South Caucasus. A licence decision would be the marker.

items.title: Türkiye sets 2028 launch for new microsatellite and 2027 for Turkic states satellite
items.summary: Turkish trade press reports a new Turkish microsatellite will launch in 2028. A joint satellite of the Turkic states is to go up in 2027. The earlier proposal of nine billion lira for 2027 has no published split.
items.why: Türkiye's programme dates now run to 2028. The funding split is still missing.

items.title: Southern Launch opens Koonibba observatory; Sunburnt Space announces largest rocket for 2027
items.summary: The Koonibba Observatory and Stargazing Facility opened in South Australia on the twenty-fourth of November. Sunburnt Space announced its largest rocket yet, for a 2027 launch.
items.why: Australia's launch sector is adding facilities and vehicles. The 2027 launch date is not yet fixed.

items.title: JAXA publishes H3 transition release in Japanese
items.summary: JAXA issued a release on the H3 transition on the twentieth of November, in Japanese only. The schedule and operator are not known.
items.why: The future of Japan's main rocket depends on this transition. No date is set.

items.title: NASA makes Moon base contract awards; proposals due eighth of December
items.summary: NASA made its Moon base awards on the ninth of November. Further proposals are due on the eighth of December.
items.why: Awards are made and a second round is open. The proposal date is the next fixed point.

audio_script:
Good morning. It is Wednesday, the twenty-fifth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Ariane 6 has put thirty-six more Amazon Leo satellites into orbit. A Pakistani astronaut has launched aboard a Chinese rocket. And Europe's BepiColombo probe is in orbit around Mercury despite an unexpected problem.

Ariane 6 has launched another thirty-six Amazon Leo satellites. ArianeGroup says the tenth Ariane 6 flight, mission VA271, delivered them on the twenty-fourth of November, after the window moved from the twenty-third. Amazon's earlier Leo launch, on a Vulcan rocket, failed on the fifteenth of November. The cause of that failure and the date of the next Vulcan flight are not known. This matters because Amazon's constellation has lost one launch provider for now, while a European launcher has delivered a large commercial batch on a rescheduled date. Note that this rests on a company statement only; we have no independent confirmation of orbit insertion in hand. The next date that matters for European launch policy is the fifteenth of December, in Rome.

In Europe, ESA says BepiColombo is safely in orbit around Mercury, despite an unexpected challenge. Spanish trade coverage mentions a fault on board. The nature of the fault is not public, and the science start date is not known. That date will show how serious the problem is. ESA's Euclid telescope has also broken its own quasar record, by forty million years. On policy, the vote of the tenth of November produced no outcome, and the MaiaSpace contract is unsigned. On the eighteenth of November the European Commission recommended that its competition fund grow five times. That funding is recommended but not decided. Rome on the fifteenth of December is the next point at which it can move.

In Ukraine, access to Starshield remains the live question. Kyiv reported further restrictions on the twelfth of November. SpaceX has made no statement. The hope of a replacement by mid-2027 is unchanged. Ukraine's front-line communications depend on a service it does not control, and no date is set for a change.

In Sweden, the national space agency has noted that Voyager 1 has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth. The agency's next national event, Rymddagen, is on the eighteenth of February, 2027. That is the next fixed Nordic marker.

In Spain, the first test of military Govsatcom access through the SpainSat NG I satellite has been carried out. Details of the test are not given. It is a first use of the EU pooled service over a national satellite, though wider Govsatcom use is not yet dated. In Italy, the government has made Iceye's offer for rocket maker Avio conditional on national security guarantees. The terms are not known. A launcher maker may pass to a foreign satellite company, and Rome's conditions will decide whether the bid proceeds.

In Kazakhstan, Amazon Leo and a Chinese rival are set to enter the satellite internet market. No start date is given, and licensing dates are not known. In Armenia, the telecom regulator and SpaceX have discussed satellite internet and mobile services. No licence has been announced. A licence decision would be the marker to watch.

In Türkiye, a new microsatellite is to launch in 2028, and a joint satellite of the Turkic states in 2027. The earlier proposal of nine billion lira for 2027 still has no published split. The funding split is the missing piece.

In China, a Pakistani astronaut, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, has launched on a Chinese rocket. Spanish press calls him the first foreign astronaut admitted to China's space station. Mission length is not given. China is opening its station to a South Asian partner, which widens its list of space partners beyond Russia. In Australia, the Koonibba Observatory and Stargazing Facility opened in South Australia on the twenty-fourth of November, and Sunburnt Space announced its largest rocket yet, for 2027. The 2027 launch date is not yet fixed. In Japan, JAXA's release of the twentieth of November on the H3 transition is in Japanese only. The schedule and operator are not known.

In the United States, NASA made its Moon base awards on the ninth of November. Further proposals are due on the eighth of December. The Vulcan cause remains unknown.

What we are tracking this week is the cause of the Vulcan failure, any SpaceX statement on Starshield, and the BepiColombo science start date. This month it is the Artemis proposals due on the eighth of December and the Rome meeting on the fifteenth of December. The heads-up date beyond that is the eighteenth of February, for Sweden's Rymddagen. That is the briefing for Wednesday, the twenty-fifth of November.

summary: ArianeGroup says Ariane 6 carried another 36 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit on its tenth flight on the twenty-fourth of November.
